collections/list#

An immutable persistent linked list.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let empty is List<string> = EmptyList();
let names = empty
    .prefix("Lovelace")
    .prefix("Hopper");

// names.first() == "Hopper"
// names.tail().first() == "Lovelace"
// empty.size() == 0

Description#

An immutable persistent linked list.

Build a list by prefixing values onto an explicitly typed empty list:

prefix() never changes the receiver. The new list shares its immutable tail with the old list, so retaining earlier versions is cheap and safe:

let one = empty.prefix("one");
let two = one.prefix("two");
// one still contains only "one"
// two contains "two", then "one"

Lists participate in ordinary iteration:

for names -> name {
    Stdout().writeln(name);
}

A list is deliberately not a Sequencing object and has no item(index) action. Finding the nth linked node requires traversal; use cursor(), for, or a genuinely indexed collection instead of disguising that cost.

first() and tail() on EmptyList throw EmptyListAccess. Calling item() or successor() on an exhausted cursor throws IterationEnded. List cursors are immutable: successor() returns a cursor for the shared tail and leaves the previous cursor unchanged.

Public API#

role List#

role List<T>

List is conceptually the conjunction of Iterating<T> and Sizing. Until the language supports role composition, the shared signatures are stated here and concrete lists explicitly implement all three roles.

cursor() is Cursor<T>

Walks from the first item.

size() is int

How many items; counting walks the list.

first() is T

The first item; EmptyListAccess when empty.

List.tail#

tail() is List<T>

The list after its first item; EmptyListAccess when empty.

List.prefix#

prefix(value is T) is List<T>

This list with value in front; the old list is shared, not copied.

object EmptyList#

object EmptyList<T> does List<T>, Iterating<T>, Sizing

The list with no items; type it to start one: let empty is List<string> = EmptyList();.
